points.title: 音乐启蒙
points.description: 勃拉姆斯1833年5月7日出生于汉堡的一个普通家庭，父亲是低音提琴手，母亲是裁缝。他从小展现出非凡的音乐天赋，父亲发现后安排他跟随著名教育家马克斯·鲍尔学习钢琴和音乐理论。10岁时开始公开演出，13岁创作了第一批钢琴作品。这段时期，他接触了汉堡丰富的音乐生活，包括歌剧和交响乐，为他后来的创作奠定了基础。同时，他也在汉堡的酒馆和舞厅演奏，这些经历让他接触到民间音乐元素，影响了他的创作风格。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Hamburg to a modest family, Brahms showed exceptional musical talent from an early age. His father, a double bass player, arranged for him to study piano and music theory with renowned educator Marx Bauer. By age 10, he was performing publicly, and by 13, had composed his first piano works. During this period, he was exposed to Hamburg's rich musical life, including opera and symphonies, which laid the foundation for his later compositions. He also performed in taverns and dance halls, exposing him to folk music elements that influenced his compositional style.

points.title: 邂逅大师
points.description: 1853年，勃拉姆斯开始了巡回演出之旅，在汉诺威遇到了著名小提琴家约阿希姆，后者成为他一生的挚友和重要支持者。约阿希姆将他引荐给了李斯特和李斯特的伴侣克拉拉·舒曼。这次会面对勃拉姆斯的职业生涯产生了决定性影响。克拉拉·舒曼成为了他最重要的精神导师和艺术知己，两人之间建立了深厚的友谊和艺术共鸣。在魏玛期间，勃拉姆斯与李斯特的浪漫主义风格产生了分歧，这促使他更加坚定地走自己的艺术道路。这一时期，他创作了《d小调钢琴协奏曲》等重要作品，确立了其独特的音乐语言。
points.descriptionEn: In 1853, Brahms began a concert tour that led him to meet renowned violinist Joseph Joachim, who became his lifelong friend and important supporter. Joachim introduced him to Franz Liszt and his companion Clara Schumann. This encounter proved decisive for Brahms' career. Clara Schumann became his most important spiritual mentor and artistic confidante, with whom he developed a deep friendship and artistic resonance. During his time in Weimar, Brahms developed artistic differences with Liszt's Romantic style, which strengthened his resolve to follow his own artistic path. During this period, he composed important works including the Piano Concerto in D minor, establishing his unique musical language.

points.title: 艺术成熟
points.description: 1863年，勃拉姆斯定居维也纳，这座城市成为他创作和生活的中心。在维也纳期间，他担任维也纳合唱团指挥，并逐渐成为欧洲最受尊敬的音乐家之一。这一时期是他创作的黄金时代，完成了《德意志安魂曲》、第一交响曲、第二交响曲等重要作品。勃拉姆斯在维也纳建立了广泛的社交圈，包括作曲家、音乐家和知识分子，这些交流丰富了他的艺术视野。他特别关注德国民间音乐传统，将其融入自己的创作中，形成了独特的古典主义风格与浪漫主义情感相结合的艺术特色。维也纳的艺术氛围和音乐传统深深影响了他的创作方向。
points.descriptionEn: Settling in Vienna in 1863, the city became the center of Brahms' creative and professional life. During his time in Vienna, he served as director of the Vienna Singakademie and gradually became one of Europe's most respected musicians. This period marked his golden age of composition, during which he completed major works including the German Requiem, First Symphony, and Second Symphony. Brahms established a wide social circle in Vienna, including composers, musicians, and intellectuals, whose exchanges enriched his artistic perspective. He particularly focused on German folk music traditions, incorporating them into his compositions to form a unique artistic style combining classical form with romantic emotion. Vienna's artistic atmosphere and musical traditions profoundly influenced his creative direction.

points.title: 巅峰创作
points.description: 1875年至1885年是勃拉姆斯创作生涯的巅峰时期。他完成了第三交响曲、第四交响曲、小提琴协奏曲、第二钢琴协奏曲等重要作品，这些作品展现了他成熟的作曲技巧和深刻的艺术思想。勃拉姆斯在这一时期获得了多项荣誉，包括剑桥大学授予的荣誉博士学位。他特别注重作品的严谨结构和内在逻辑，同时又不失浪漫主义的情感表达。这一时期，他与克拉拉·舒曼的关系经历了复杂的变化，但艺术上的交流更加深入。勃拉姆斯的作品在这一时期获得了广泛认可，被视为连接古典与浪漫主义桥梁的重要人物。他在维也纳的音乐会大获成功，确立了作为当时最重要作曲家的地位。
points.descriptionEn: The period from 1875 to 1885 marked the peak of Brahms' compositional career. He completed major works including his Third and Fourth Symphonies, Violin Concerto, and Second Piano Concerto, showcasing his mature compositional techniques and profound artistic ideas. During this period, Brahms received numerous honors, including an honorary doctorate from Cambridge University. He particularly emphasized rigorous structure and internal logic in his works while maintaining Romantic emotional expression. His relationship with Clara Schumann underwent complex changes during this time, but their artistic exchange deepened. Brahms' works gained widespread recognition during this period, establishing him as a crucial figure bridging classical and Romantic traditions. His concerts in Vienna were highly successful, cementing his status as one of the most important composers of his time.

points.title: 晚年创作
points.description: 1886年至1897年是勃拉姆斯的晚年创作时期。尽管健康状况逐渐恶化，他仍然创作了大量重要作品，包括《二十一首匈牙利舞曲》、《小提琴奏鸣曲》和《单簧管五重奏》等。这一时期，勃拉姆斯的作品更加内省和深刻，展现了对生命和艺术的终极思考。他特别关注室内乐创作，创作了一系列优秀的钢琴小品和室内乐作品。勃拉姆斯晚年仍然活跃于维也纳的音乐界，担任多个音乐协会的荣誉职务，并指导年轻音乐家。1897年4月3日，勃拉姆斯在维也纳逝世，享年63岁。他的去世标志着浪漫主义音乐时代的终结，他的作品和音乐思想对后世产生了深远影响，被视为德奥音乐传统的集大成者。
points.descriptionEn: The period from 1886 to 1897 marked Brahms' late creative phase. Despite declining health, he continued to compose numerous important works, including the Twenty Hungarian Dances, Violin Sonatas, and Clarinet Quintets. During this period, Brahms' works became more introspective and profound, reflecting his ultimate thoughts on life and art. He focused particularly on chamber music composition, creating a series of excellent piano pieces and chamber works. Brahms remained active in Vienna's musical community in his later years, holding honorary positions in various music associations and mentoring young musicians. He died in Vienna on April 3, 1897, at the age of 63. His death marked the end of the Romantic era in music, and his works and musical ideas had a profound influence on later generations, establishing him as the culmination of the German-Austrian musical tradition.

supporter.zh: 勃拉姆斯被视为古典音乐传统的守护者和革新者。他继承了巴赫、贝多芬的严谨结构，同时注入了浪漫主义的情感深度。他的作品以其完美的形式、丰富的和声与深刻的情感表达而著称，被誉为'贝多芬之后最伟大的交响作曲家'。勃拉姆斯对民间音乐的深入研究，使他的作品具有独特的民族特色。他一生追求艺术完美，拒绝妥协，这种坚持使他成为音乐史上最具影响力的作曲家之一，对后世音乐创作产生了深远影响。
supporter.en: Brahms is regarded as a guardian and innovator of the classical music tradition. He inherited the rigorous structures of Bach and Beethoven while infusing them with Romantic emotional depth. His works are celebrated for their perfect form, rich harmonies, and profound emotional expression, earning him the title 'greatest symphonic composer after Beethoven.' His deep study of folk music gave his works unique national characteristics. His lifelong pursuit of artistic perfection and refusal to compromise made him one of the most influential composers in music history, with a profound impact on future musical creations.

critic.zh: 批评者认为勃拉姆斯过于保守，缺乏创新精神。他被指责为'反动派'，固守古典形式而拒绝接受新的音乐语言。一些评论家认为他的作品过于学术化，缺乏即兴性和自发性，情感表达受到过度控制。此外，勃拉姆斯对瓦格纳等创新派作曲家的公开批评被视为狭隘和偏执。他的个人生活也被批评为过于封闭和孤僻，缺乏与时代的积极互动。这些批评者认为，勃拉姆斯虽然技巧精湛，但未能完全突破传统的束缚，限制了其艺术成就的高度。
critic.en: Critics argue that Brahms was overly conservative and lacked innovative spirit. He was criticized as a 'reactionary' who clung to classical forms while rejecting new musical languages. Some commentators认为 his works were too academic, lacking improvisation and spontaneity, with emotional expression overly controlled. Additionally, his public criticism of innovative composers like Wagner was seen as narrow and dogmatic. His personal life was also criticized as overly reclusive and isolated, lacking positive engagement with his era. These critics argue that while Brahms possessed exceptional technical skill, he failed to fully break free from traditional constraints, limiting the height of his artistic achievements.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，勃拉姆斯被定义为连接古典与浪漫主义的关键桥梁。他既尊重传统形式，又融入浪漫主义的情感表达，形成了独特的艺术风格。历史学界认为，勃拉姆斯代表了19世纪音乐传统的最高成就之一，与瓦格纳形成鲜明对比，代表了音乐发展的另一条路径。在流行文化中，勃拉姆斯常被描绘为严肃、内敛的艺术家形象，他的作品被广泛用于电影、广告等媒体，成为古典音乐普及的重要代表。他的生平故事，特别是与克拉拉·舒曼的复杂关系，也成为音乐史上的传奇话题，体现了艺术家个人生活与创作的交织。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Brahms is defined as a crucial bridge connecting classical and Romantic traditions. He respected traditional forms while incorporating Romantic emotional expression, creating a unique artistic style. Historians consider Brahms one of the highest achievements of 19th-century musical tradition, forming a stark contrast with Wagner and representing an alternative path in musical development. In popular culture, Brahms is often portrayed as a serious, reserved artist, and his works are widely used in films, advertisements, and other media, becoming an important representative of classical music popularization. His life story, particularly his complex relationship with Clara Schumann, has become a legendary topic in music history, illustrating the interweaving of an artist's personal life and creative work.

self.zh: 没有比不懈努力更好的天赋了。
self.en: There is no genius but the genius of perseverance.

others.zh: 勃拉姆斯的音乐是德意志精神的最高体现，它既深刻又崇高，既充满力量又无比温柔。
others.en: Brahms' music is the highest expression of the German spirit—it is both profound and sublime, both powerful and infinitely tender.
